title: Military Maneuver
statementMd:
A military maneuver is going on a two-dimensional Cartesian plane, and 𝑛n enemy targets are hiding somewhere on the battlefield, whose locations are known to our headquarters.

Our headquarters will airdrop a beacon in a rectangular region with sides parallel to the coordinate axes uniformly at random to expose all the enemy targets to our troops on the battlefield so that our troops can surround all the enemy targets. The bottom-left corner of the region is at coordinate (𝑥𝑙,𝑦𝑙)(xl,yl) while the top-right corner is at coordinate (𝑥𝑟,𝑦𝑟)(xr,yr).

After being dropped, the beacon will firstly receive two parameters 𝑟r and 𝑅R that satisfy 0≤𝑟≤𝑅0≤r≤R from our headquarters, then scan an annulus region, that is, the region lying between two concentric circles, where the radius of the inner circle is 𝑟r and that of the outer circle is 𝑅R, and finally mark those enemy targets hiding in the scanned region (including the boundary).

However, the beacon can only scan a unit area in a unit of time, and the commander would like to know the expected minimum time for the beacon to scan the designated annulus region so that it can mark all the enemy targets.

## Input

The first line contains four integers 𝑥𝑙,𝑦𝑙,𝑥𝑟xl,yl,xr, and 𝑦𝑟yr (−10000≤𝑥𝑙,𝑦𝑙,𝑥𝑟,𝑦𝑟≤10000−10000≤xl,yl,xr,yr≤10000, 𝑥𝑙<𝑥𝑟xl<xr, 𝑦𝑙<𝑦𝑟yl<yr), denoting the coordinates of the bottom-left and the top-right corners of the rectangular region where the beacon will be dropped.

The second line contains a single integer 𝑛n (2≤𝑛≤20002≤n≤2000), denoting the number of enemy targets on the battlefield.

Each of the following 𝑛n lines contains two integers 𝑥x and 𝑦y (−10000≤𝑥,𝑦≤10000−10000≤x,y≤10000), denoting an enemy target located at coordinate (𝑥,𝑦)(x,y).

It is guaranteed that no two enemy targets share the same locations.

## Output

Output a single real number, indicating the expected minimum time for the beacon to scan the designated annulus region.

Your answer is acceptable if its absolute or relative error does not exceed 10−610−6. Formally speaking, suppose that your output is 𝑎a and the jury's answer is 𝑏b, your output is accepted if and only if |𝑎−𝑏|max(1,|𝑏|)≤10−6|a−b|max(1,|b|)≤10−6.

## Note

In the first sample case, if the beacon is dropped to (0.5,1.5)(0.5,1.5), the minimum time as well as the minimum area of the feasible annulus region is 4𝜋4π. The expected minimum time when the beacon dropped in the rectangular region uniformly at random is 38𝜋38π.
